ledger.claim: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances. Trip TRP-05009 records an actual distance of 10.0 km against a recommended-route distance of 8.5 km, a deviation of 1.50 km, which is over the 1.0 km tolerance that POL-RD-22 sets. The trip record's own derived block carries that figure (1.50 km) and the tolerance flag (within_tolerance: false), so no geometry needs to be recomputed here. A deviation over tolerance is the gateway to the refund matrix in POL-RD-24, and the rider's contested charge sits on that excess distance.

The GPS trace confirms the route actually taken, which is the only use POL-RD-22 permits a trace to be put to. It shows the vehicle running Woodlands Square, Woodlands Avenue 2, then Woodlands Road from 15:51:49 and rejoining at Bukit Panjang Road and Petir Road, exactly as the trip events record: route_deviation_detected at 15:51:59 (vehicle took Woodlands Road instead of the recommended BKE) and route_rejoined at 16:03:01. The detour is real and lasted roughly eleven minutes; it is not a measurement artefact of a sparse trace, because the policy expressly directs the distances to be read from the trip record and the trace only to show which route was taken and when.

Disclosure first, as POL-GEN-02 requires: the traffic-advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-05009-01 is MISSING, its admissibility weight_multiplier is 0.0 and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT, so it carries no fact and I do not present it as proving anything about traffic. Its absence is decisive against the driver all the same. POL-RD-23 makes a reroute traffic-justified only where traffic data for the recommended route at the trip time shows congestion, an incident or a closure, and its closing sentence is explicit: 'A driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute.' The driver's only support is his own bare assertion in chat — 'BKE got accident near Dairy Farm, I take Woodlands Road ok?' (MSG-05009-003) and his counterparty statement — and an assertion is precisely what POL-RD-23 refuses to accept. On this record the reroute is not traffic-justified.

The rider did not merely accept a reroute; he accepted one on the strength of an asserted accident that nothing in the record corroborates. The claim of an accident rests entirely on MSG-05009-003, and the only artifact that could have confirmed or refuted a BKE incident in that window, the LTA traffic record, is the one the platform failed to retrieve (EV-ADVIS-05009-01, MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT). The rider's own words are that he agreed because he believed the driver and could find no accident news afterwards. That reliance, on an unverified premise, is why the acknowledgement cannot be treated as a free pass for the detour.

I do not contest the notice limb, and I say so plainly: the driver notified the rider by in-app chat at 15:49:39, before the point of deviation at 15:51:59, with a brief reason, and the rider answered 'ok can' at 15:49:59 — so POL-RD-21's inform-and-acknowledge requirement is met. But notice is not the whole of the matrix. Row (a) of POL-RD-24 requires the reroute to be BOTH traffic-justified AND informed-and-agreed; rows (b) and (c) also require traffic justification. Every no-refund path runs through justification. Since justification fails on POL-RD-23, the acknowledged chat cannot buy the driver a NO_ACTION outcome: it removes the notification objection, not the refund.

The case therefore falls squarely in row (d) of POL-RD-24: not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km, so the excess distance fare is refunded in full. The clause fixes the arithmetic — deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, no surge, rounded to the cent — and the fare breakdown carries both inputs: 1.50 km (EV-TRIP-05009, per POL-RD-22) times 0.72 SGD per km = 1.08 SGD, which is the excess_distance_fare_sgd figure the payments ledger itself derives under POL-RD-24. The rider filed this dispute, the fare is recorded as CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd of 0.00, so a PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.08 SGD is a rider win: it takes 1.08 SGD of the disputed charge off the rider, whereas NO_ACTION would leave the whole charge standing against him.

There is no obstacle to the AI deciding this case on the merits, so the refund above can issue without escalation. The contested amount is 3.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence; both profiles carry fraud_flags of 0, evidencing no 0.95 uplift; and the deviation of 1.50 km is within POL-RD-25's 2.0 km ceiling, so even if that held limb were applied the case would stay with the AI. Nothing in POL-GEN-22, POL-RD-25 or the policy thresholds requires this dispute to be sent away from the merits.

In the alternative only, if the judge were to read the empty LTA artifact not as a failed justification under POL-RD-23 but as an open question of fact, then POL-GEN-26 requires the case to be escalated, because the traffic justification is a fact POL-RD-24 needs and the evidence that would carry it is missing. I accept that artifact's weight of 0.0 and its MISSING_ARTIFACT code. Even on that reading the rider does better than on NO_ACTION: under POL-GEN-03 an ESCALATE ruling means no monetary outcome issues and the amount is held rather than collected, so the 1.08 SGD the rider says was wrongly charged is not confirmed against him while the traffic question is checked.

The driver gave the rider in-app notice before he deviated, which is what POL-RD-21 requires. MSG-05009-003 — 'Hi, BKE got accident near Dairy Farm, I take Woodlands Road ok?' — was sent at 15:49:39 through the IN_APP channel and read at 15:49:50, and the trip record's own derived messages_during_trip block lists that message and the rider's reply as in-trip messages under POL-RD-21. The vehicle's first Woodlands Road fix is not until 15:51:49, so the notice preceded the deviation rather than following it. The chat-log artifact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and its 4 entries match trip_record.chat_message_count.

The rider acknowledged the reroute in the same channel and in advance of it. MSG-05009-004, 'ok can', was sent at 15:49:59 — twenty seconds after the driver's message — while the platform's own deviation event is timestamped 15:51:59 and the first Woodlands Road fix 15:51:49. POL-RD-21 provides that where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the deviation is agreed; on this record the Woodlands Road leg is an agreed deviation, and the rider cannot now treat as unconsented the extra distance she accepted while sitting in the car.

The only traffic data in this record is EV-ADVIS-05009-01 and it is MISSING; I disclose that it carries the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and a weight_multiplier of 0.0, and that under POL-GEN-02 a MISSING artifact carries no fact. Its own derived block records why: the platform's request to the LTA historical traffic feed timed out and was not retried, so the record is 'silent on traffic on the recommended route; this is not a finding of no traffic'. Traffic justification under POL-RD-23 therefore cannot be established either way on this record — the driver's assertion of a jam alone would not justify the reroute, but neither does an absent advisory establish that the BKE was clear.

The rider's case rests on her own search for accident news after the trip, which is not the traffic data POL-RD-23 requires (a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY intersecting the recommended route and overlapping the trip window) and says nothing about this trip's road conditions at 15:50 on 23 August 2026. Under POL-GEN-26 no outcome is inferred from the absence of evidence, so her failure to find a news report no more shows the BKE was clear than the missing LTA record shows it was congested. The rider has produced no traffic data; she has produced the absence of a search result.

ledger.claim: Escalation is the driver-protective outcome here, and it is the outcome POL-GEN-03 defines: ESCALATE is terminal, no monetary outcome issues, and the amount is held. The ledger shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so there is nothing to restore and the metered fare of 14.05 SGD stays where it is while a human reviewer retrieves the LTA feed that the platform failed to obtain. NO_ACTION would equally leave the charge standing, because the rider filed and the charge has not been refunded.

If the judge nevertheless finds that a refund row applies, POL-RD-24 fixes the refund at the excess distance fare — deviation_km times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge — which on this record is 1.50 km x 0.72 SGD = 1.08 SGD, not the 3.50 SGD the rider asks for. The 3.15 SGD time fare for 17.5 minutes is not part of that measure, and FULL_REFUND under POL-GEN-03 would require the filer to be entirely right, which on an in-app agreed deviation she is not. The rider's exposure is at most a 1.08 SGD partial refund on a 14.05 SGD fare.

The deviation itself is minor and was not an abandonment of the route. On POL-RD-22's recorded-distance method it is 1.50 km on an 8.5 km recommended route (10.0 km actual less 8.5 km optimal), and the driver-device trace shows one continuous detour along Woodlands Road, Bukit Panjang Road and Petir Road, rejoining the recommended route at Petir Road at 16:03:01 before drop-off at Hillion Mall. Even under the v2.1 6.2 limb held in POL-RD-25 — which is not applied in this case, ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied being false — a 2.0 km ceiling would not be crossed.

ruling.explanation:
The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and the drafts did not agree, so no ruling was carried and the dispute is escalated. Each draft proposed:
- draft 1 (sampled): PARTIAL_REFUND, amount_sgd 1.08, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
- draft 2 (sampled): abstained -- DRAFT_CLAUSE_UNRESOLVED: 'POL-NS-24' does not resolve in the loaded policy; DRAFT_CLAUSE_UNRESOLVED: 'POL-NS-25' does not resolve in the loaded policy; DRAFT_CLAUSE_UNRESOLVED: 'POL-NS-22' does not resolve in the loaded policy
- draft 3 (sampled): ESCALATE, amount_sgd null, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
- draft 4 (position_swapped): PARTIAL_REFUND, amount_sgd 1.08, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
At most 2 of 3 valid drafts agreed and 3 were needed. The best supported answer is not published as a ruling: a ruling has to be the panel's, not one draft's.
